products.name: Oat Milk Cream Cleanser

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Glycerin, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Avena Sativa Kernel Flour, Cetearyl Alcohol, Glyceryl Stearate, Coco-Glucoside, Panthenol, Sodium Benzoate, Citric Acid

products.short: A soft cream cleanser with colloidal oat that leaves dry skin comfortable, never tight.
description: Massage a fingertip of cream over dry skin, then add a little water and it turns milky and lifts away sunscreen, make-up and the day. It rinses clean without the squeak that tells you a cleanser has taken too much.
Colloidal oat calms and glycerin holds water in the skin, so it suits dry and sensitive skin morning and night. Follow with toner, or go straight to your serum.

products.name: Green Tea Gel Cleanser

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate, Glycerin, Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract, Coco-Betaine, Salicylic Acid, Panthenol, Xanthan Gum, Sodium Benzoate, Citric Acid

products.short: A low-foam gel with green tea and a touch of salicylic acid for oily, breakout-prone skin.
description: A clear gel that works into a light lather and clears oil and sunscreen without stripping. Half a percent of salicylic acid works inside the pore while green tea calms the look of redness.
Use it morning and night on oily or combination skin, or in the evening only if your skin is drier in winter.

products.name: Melting Cleansing Balm

specs.Ingredients: Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Camellia Oleifera Seed Oil, Polyglyceryl-4 Oleate, Helianthus Annuus Seed Wax, Avena Sativa Kernel Oil, Tocopherol

products.short: A solid balm that melts into oil on contact and dissolves make-up, then rinses off milky.
description: Scoop a little with the spatula and warm it between your fingers: it melts into a silky oil that dissolves long-wear make-up and sunscreen. Add water and it turns milky and rinses away clean.
The first step of an evening double cleanse. Follow with the gel or cream cleanser.

products.name: Kaolin Clay Mask

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Kaolin, Glycerin, Niacinamide, Bentonite, Cetearyl Alcohol, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Xanthan Gum, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: A weekly clay mask that lifts oil from the pores and leaves skin matte, not dry.
description: Spread a thin, even layer over clean skin, avoiding the eyes, and rinse after ten minutes, before it cracks. Kaolin absorbs excess oil while niacinamide keeps the skin barrier comfortable.
Once or twice a week, after cleansing and before your serum.

products.name: Rosewater Hydrating Toner

specs.Ingredients: Rosa Damascena Flower Water, Aqua, Glycerin, Panthenol, Betaine, Allantoin, Sodium Benzoate, Citric Acid

products.short: A rose water toner with panthenol that soothes and preps skin for serum.
description: Pour a little into your palms and press it into clean skin. Distilled rose water and panthenol leave skin soft and slightly damp, which is exactly how hyaluronic acid likes to find it.
Gentle enough for twice a day, morning and night.

products.name: AHA 7% Glow Tonic

specs.Key actives: Glycolic acid 5% | Lactic acid 2% | Kiwi fruit extract
specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Glycolic Acid, Lactic Acid, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Actinidia Chinensis Fruit Extract, Sodium Hydroxide, Glycerin, Panthenol, Tocopherol, Sodium Benzoate

products.short: Seven per cent of fruit and sugar acids at pH 3.6, with kiwi, for smoother, brighter-looking skin.
description: Sweep over clean, dry skin with a cotton round in the evening, avoiding the eye area. Glycolic and lactic acid loosen the dull surface layer so it sheds sooner; kiwi extract and aloe keep the skin calm while they work.
Start two or three evenings a week and use sunscreen every morning. Keep it apart from retinal: alternate the nights.

products.name: Centella Calming Essence

specs.Ingredients: Centella Asiatica Leaf Water, Aqua, Glycerin, Panthenol, Butylene Glycol, Madecassoside, Sodium Hyaluronate, Ethylhexylglycerin

products.short: A silky essence of centella water that calms the look of redness and leaves skin plump.
description: Pour a few drops into your palms and press into skin after cleansing. Centella water and panthenol are light as water but leave a soft, bouncy finish under serum and cream.
Layer it twice on days your skin feels hot or tight.

products.name: Hyaluronic Water Serum

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Sodium Hyaluronate, Hydrolyzed Hyaluronic Acid, Panthenol, Glycerin, Pentylene Glycol, Ethylhexylglycerin, Citric Acid

products.short: Hyaluronic acid at two molecular weights with 5% panthenol. Layers under everything.
description: Two sizes of hyaluronic acid draw water into the surface of the skin and just below it, while panthenol soothes. Apply three or four drops to damp skin, then seal it in with moisturiser.
It plays well with every other active, morning and night.

products.name: Niacinamide 10% + Zinc Serum

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Niacinamide, Pentylene Glycol, Zinc PCA, Dimethyl Isosorbide, Tamarindus Indica Seed Gum, Xanthan Gum, Ethoxydiglycol, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Ten per cent niacinamide with zinc for oily skin, visible pores and an uneven tone.
description: A light, fast-absorbing serum for skin that shines by lunchtime. Niacinamide supports the barrier and evens the look of tone; zinc helps balance oil.
Use a few drops morning and night after toner. If your skin is sensitive, start once a day.

products.name: Vitamin C 15% Brightening Serum

specs.Key actives: Ascorbic acid 15% | Vitamin E 1% | Ferulic acid 0.5%
specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Ascorbic Acid, Ethoxydiglycol, Propylene Glycol, Tocopherol, Ferulic Acid, Triethanolamine, Sodium Hyaluronate, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Pure vitamin C at 15% with vitamins E and ferulic acid, for brighter-looking skin by day.
description: Ascorbic acid works best at a low pH, so this one sits at 3.2. Vitamin E and ferulic acid keep it stable and help it defend skin through the day.
Apply in the morning under sunscreen. A slight tingle is normal. The amber bottle keeps out light; use it within six months of opening.

products.name: Retinal 0.1% Night Serum

specs.Ingredients: Squalane, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Retinal, Tocopherol, Bisabolol, Simmondsia Chinensis Seed Oil, Helianthus Annuus Seed Oil

products.short: Retinal, one step from retinoic acid, in a squalane base for smoother texture. Night only.
description: Retinal converts to retinoic acid in a single step, so 0.1% does the work of a much stronger retinol. Squalane and bisabolol keep the skin comfortable while it adjusts.
Start two nights a week on dry skin, then build up. Never on the same night as acids, and always sunscreen the next morning. Not for use during pregnancy.

products.name: Calendula Face Oil

specs.Ingredients: Squalane, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Calendula Officinalis Flower Extract, Helianthus Annuus Seed Oil, Tocopherol

products.short: Plant squalane with calendula: a featherlight oil that softens and calms without shine.
description: Squalane is close to the oil skin makes itself, so it sinks in quickly and leaves no greasy film; calendula soothes dry, tight patches. Press two drops over moisturiser at night, or mix one into your foundation.
Squalane is stable, so the oil will not turn rancid, and it suits even oily skin.

products.name: Peptide Eye Cream

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Glycerin, Caffeine, Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1, Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7, Squalane, Cetearyl Alcohol, Sodium Hyaluronate, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Peptides and caffeine in a light cream for the look of puffiness and fine lines around the eyes.
description: Tap a rice-grain amount around the orbital bone with your ring finger, morning and night. Caffeine helps the look of morning puffiness; peptides support firmer-looking skin over time.
Light enough to wear under concealer.

products.name: Ceramide Barrier Cream

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Glycerin, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Ceramide NP, Ceramide AP, Ceramide EOP, Cholesterol, Phytosphingosine, Butyrospermum Parkii Butter, Cetearyl Alcohol, Sodium Hyaluronate, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Three ceramides with cholesterol and fatty acids, in the ratio skin uses, for a stressed barrier.
description: A rich, cushiony cream that holds the skin barrier together while strong actives do their work. Ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids are the lipids skin is made of; together they help it keep water in.
Use it morning and night as the last step before sunscreen. The 100 ml jar has the lower price per 100 ml.

products.name: Daily Gel Cream

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Glycerin, Niacinamide, Squalane, Sodium Hyaluronate, Carbomer, Allantoin, Tromethamine, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: A weightless gel cream that hydrates oily skin without shine.
description: A cooling, water-light gel that disappears in seconds and leaves a soft matte finish. Niacinamide balances, hyaluronic acid hydrates.
Morning and night, before sunscreen in the day.

products.name: Overnight Recovery Mask

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Butyrospermum Parkii Butter, Glycerin, Squalane, Palmitoyl Tripeptide-5, Lavandula Angustifolia Flower Water, Cetearyl Alcohol, Tocopherol, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: A rich sleeping cream with peptides and shea that works while you sleep.
description: Smooth a generous layer over your evening routine as the last step. By morning, skin is soft, plump and rested-looking.
Two or three nights a week, or every night in winter.

products.name: Mineral Sun Fluid SPF 50

specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Zinc Oxide, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Niacinamide, Polyglyceryl-3 Polyricinoleate, Glycerin, Tocopherol, Magnesium Sulfate, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Broad-spectrum mineral protection in a sheer fluid that leaves no white cast.
description: Twenty per cent non-nano zinc oxide filters UVA and UVB light, in a fluid that blends clear on most skin tones. Niacinamide keeps sensitive skin calm under it.
Apply generously as the last step every morning, about half a teaspoon for the face and neck, and reapply through the day outdoors.

products.name: Daily Sun Cream SPF 30

specs.Key actives: UVA and UVB filters | Vitamin E 0.5%
specs.Ingredients: Aqua, Homosalate, Butyl Methoxydibenzoylmethane, Ethylhexyl Salicylate, Glycerin, Tocopherol, Cetearyl Alcohol, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: An everyday SPF 30 lotion for face and body that sinks in fast.
description: A light lotion for days in town: it absorbs quickly, sits well under make-up and comes in a size that also covers arms and neck.
For long days outdoors, choose SPF 50.

products.name: Aloe After-Sun Gel

specs.Ingredients: Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Aqua, Glycerin, Panthenol, Allantoin, Carbomer, Sodium Hydroxide, Phenoxyethanol

products.short: Ninety per cent aloe vera with panthenol to cool and comfort skin after the sun.
description: Keep it in the fridge for the coolest relief. Smooth over face and body after a day outside; it sinks in without stickiness.

products.name: Satin Lipstick

specs.Ingredients: Ricinus Communis Seed Oil, Euphorbia Cerifera Cera, Butyrospermum Parkii Butter, Tocopherol, Mica, CI 77491, CI 15850

products.short: A creamy satin lipstick in four wearable shades that stays comfortable all day.
description: Pigment-dense colour in one swipe, with shea butter and vitamin E so lips never feel dry. The satin finish has a soft sheen, not a gloss.
Rosewood is a muted pink, Brick a warm terracotta, Plum Noir a deep berry and Coral a bright peach.

products.name: Tinted Lip Balm SPF 15

specs.Ingredients: Ricinus Communis Seed Oil, Euphorbia Cerifera Cera, Butyrospermum Parkii Butter, Zinc Oxide, Tocopherol, CI 77491

products.short: A sheer wash of colour over shea butter, with SPF 15 for everyday lips.
description: Somewhere between a balm and a lipstick: a hint of rosy colour, a soft shine and protection for the lips on sunny days. Reapply as often as you like.

products.name: Nourishing Lip Oil

specs.Ingredients: Simmondsia Chinensis Seed Oil, Polyisobutene, Rosa Canina Fruit Oil, Tocopherol, Mica

products.short: A glossy lip oil that cushions and conditions without stickiness.
description: A clear, glossy oil with jojoba and rosehip. Wear it alone for shine or over lipstick to soften the finish.

products.name: Skin Tint Stick SPF 20

specs.Ingredients: Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Zinc Oxide, Euphorbia Cerifera Cera, Squalane, Niacinamide, Silica, Tocopherol, Iron Oxides

Swipe over the cheeks, forehead and chin, then blend with your fingers. For full sun protection, wear your sunscreen underneath.

products.name: Cream Blush, Petal

products.short: A petal-pink cream blush in a mirrored compact that melts in with a fingertip.
description: Tap onto the cheeks and blend upwards. Build it from a flush to a bold cheek; it sets to a soft, dewy finish that lasts. A dab doubles as lip colour.

products.name: Volume Defining Mascara

products.short: A tapered brush that separates as it coats, for volume without clumps.

Replace it six months after opening.

products.name: Translucent Setting Powder

products.name: Eyeshadow Palette, Dusk

products.name: Dry Body Oil

products.name: Barrier Hand Balm

content.heading: We read the label, so you can too
content.text: A skincare shop that lists every formula in full.

items: Buying skincare had become a guessing game: beautiful bottles, vague promises and ingredient lists in print too small to read. So we do it the other way round.

Every product we stock is listed by what is in it: the key actives and their strength, the pH, the texture and the full ingredient list. Then it is numbered by where it goes in a routine, and priced per 100 ml so a small bottle and a big one compare fairly.

items.title: Every active, with its strength
items.text: A name without a number tells you very little, so every label shows both.

items.title: The pH, where it matters
items.text: Acids and vitamin C work in a narrow range, so we print it.

items.title: A fair price per 100 ml
items.text: Sizes differ. The price per 100 ml lets you compare like with like.

items.title: Numbered by routine step
items.text: Cleanse, tone, treat, moisturise and protect: every product knows its place.

items.heading: Small batches, short lists
items.text: Our formulas are made in small batches by an independent laboratory, with as few ingredients as each one needs. Every bottle carries a batch number and the date it was filled.

ingredients.title: Ingredient glossary
content: The actives you will meet most often in our formulas, in plain words: what each one is for, when to use it and what it gets along with.
A sugar the skin makes itself. Applied to damp skin it draws in water and holds it, so skin looks plumper and feels less tight. Morning and night; pairs with everything.
Vitamin B3. Supports the skin barrier and helps even the look of tone and pores. 5% suits most skin; 10% suits oilier skin. Morning and night.
Ascorbic acid helps defend skin through the day and brightens its look over time. It works best at a low pH, so use it in the morning under sunscreen.
A form of vitamin A one step from retinoic acid, so it works at lower strengths. Smooths the look of texture and fine lines. Night only; start twice a week.
An AHA that loosens the dull surface layer so it sheds sooner. Strength and pH decide how much it does. Evenings, two or three times a week, not on retinal nights.
The lipids that hold skin cells together. Creams with ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids help a stressed barrier recover. The safe partner for strong actives.
A mineral filter that reflects and absorbs UVA and UVB light. Modern non-nano grades leave little or no white cast.

faq.title: Questions
content: How to read our labels, how to use the formulas together, and how orders work.
What does the open jar with a number mean?
It is the period after opening: 12M means the formula stays at its best for twelve months once opened.
Why is there a price per 100 ml?
Bottles come in many sizes. The price per 100 ml, or per 100 g for balms and powders, lets you compare fairly. Packs of 10 ml or less show their size only.
What do the step numbers mean?
Each skincare product is numbered by where it goes in a routine: 01 cleanse, 02 tone, 03 treat, 04 moisturise and 05 protect.
Can I use vitamin C and retinal together?
Use them apart: vitamin C in the morning under sunscreen, retinal at night.
Apply a little behind the ear or on the inner arm once a day for three days. If there is no redness or itching, start using it on your face.

how-to-layer-serums.title: How to layer serums without wasting them
how-to-layer-serums.excerpt: Thinnest to thickest, one active at a time: the order that lets every serum do its job.
content: A serum can only work if it reaches the skin. Put a thick cream on first and the watery serum on top, and most of it sits on the surface. The rule that fixes this is simple: thinnest to thickest.
Cleanse, then pat the skin almost dry.
Toner or essence, pressed in with your palms.
Watery serums first: hyaluronic acid, niacinamide.
Oil-based serums and treatments next: retinal, squalane.
Moisturiser to seal it all in, and sunscreen last in the morning.
Two strong actives on the same night, such as an acid and retinal, add irritation, not results. Alternate them instead, and keep hyaluronic acid and ceramides as the calm in between.

sunscreen-every-morning.title: Why sunscreen is the step that counts
sunscreen-every-morning.excerpt: Every other step works better when you protect it. Here is how much to use, and when.
content: Vitamin C, retinal and acids all make more of a difference when the skin is protected from the light that undoes their work. Sunscreen is the last step of every morning routine, whatever the weather.
About half a teaspoon for the face and neck: more than most people use. Two finger lengths is a good guide.
Mineral filters such as zinc oxide reflect and absorb light; other filters absorb it. Both work. Choose the texture you will wear every day.

reading-an-ingredient-list.title: How to read an ingredient list in five minutes
reading-an-ingredient-list.excerpt: The order means something, Latin names hide familiar plants, and the first five tell you most of the story.
content: Ingredient lists use the INCI system, the same names in every country. They look forbidding, but three rules make them readable.
Ingredients are listed from most to least, down to 1%. Below that they can come in any order.
Plants go by their Latin names: Avena Sativa is oat, Rosa Damascena is rose.
The first five ingredients usually make up most of the formula.
That is why our labels also show the key actives with their strength: the list tells you what is in it, the strength tells you how much.

starting-retinal.title: Starting retinal: a slow, steady plan
starting-retinal.excerpt: Twice a week, then every other night, then most nights: how to get the results without the flaking.
content: Retinal is one of the most effective ingredients for smoother-looking skin, and one of the easiest to overdo. The answer is patience.
Weeks one and two: two nights a week, on dry skin, after moisturiser if you are sensitive.
Weeks three and four: every other night.
After that: most nights, if your skin is comfortable.
Wear sunscreen every morning, keep acids for other nights, and give it twelve weeks before you judge it.
